findings.suggestion: Keep извини for a familiar singular addressee; consider извините for a polite stranger-facing apology, coordinated with 0266
findings.reason: Извини is a normal informal apology, not an error. The bank already teaches polite извините at 0266. English sorry does not signal the familiar singular register; any default change must preserve the apology versus attention-getting context. Current 0005 distractors do not include 0266.

findings.suggestion: Keep огонь for fire/flame; if the intended safety warning is a fire incident, review пожар across languages
findings.reason: Огонь names fire in general. A shouted emergency warning ordinarily needs Пожар. The Japanese 火事 explicitly names a fire incident while English fire and Latvian uguns are broader. Do not replace a useful general meaning solely because the block is Safety; decide the intended sense. No competing fire translation is in the current choices.

findings.suggestion: Consider номер экстренной помощи for an explicitly understood emergency-service phone number
findings.reason: Экстренный номер is understandable but compressed; the learner should know it means a phone number for emergency help, not an urgent identifier. This is a clarity recommendation, not a claim of incorrect grammar or measured rarity.

findings.suggestion: Keep школьник and label English school pupil/student at school
findings.reason: Russian школьник and Latvian skolēns identify a school pupil; English student also covers university students. Russian студент would change the intended school-level meaning rather than simply improve style. No current competing correct answer was found.

findings.suggestion: Keep рука for arm; record that it can also mean hand
findings.reason: Рука covers both arm and hand in everyday Russian. The intended arm sense is fine; no hand concept is currently an answer choice here. The actual 0131 palm item has рука as a distractor, but palm is specifically ладонь, so this is not being labelled an established double-answer failure.

findings.suggestion: Clarify the whole-limb/anatomical sense of нога and replace the 0135 distractor for affected directions
findings.reason: Actual RU→EN question 0134 presents leg as correct and foot (0135) as a distractor. Gramota explicitly also defines нога as стопа человека, so foot is defensible for the bare Russian prompt. RU→LV likewise presents kāja and pēda. Keep the useful нога and стопа distinction with context; do not substitute a rare synonym. The reverse 0135 question does not currently offer 0134.

findings.suggestion: Keep живот for belly/abdomen; label English stomach as the everyday belly sense
findings.reason: Живот is abdomen/belly; stomach can also name the internal organ желудок. Latvian vēders supports the belly sense. Preserve the practical belly meaning instead of making an anatomical correction without deciding the sense. No желудок distractor is present.

findings.suggestion: Consider высокая температура for the practical symptom fever; retain лихорадка if the medical term is intended
findings.reason: Лихорадка correctly denotes a feverish condition, often with chills; it is not a mistranslation. Высокая температура is an easier everyday symptom report for a beginner. This naturalness preference remains editorial. A later change must preserve symptom versus ordinary weather temperature (0350).

findings.suggestion: хочу пить (or мне хочется пить), with the personal-need phrase sense agreed across languages
findings.reason: Испытывающий жажду literally describes someone experiencing thirst, but the participial wording is cumbersome as a survival default. Хочу пить directly expresses the need and reuses пить. It changes the surface form from an adjective to a personal phrase, so compare with the existing Japanese 喉が渇いた and agree the pedagogical form before implementation. The dictionary supports the thirst sense; the preferred teaching default is editorial.

findings.suggestion: Keep шапка for a soft/knitted cap; clarify broad English hat
findings.reason: Шапка is a common practical word, especially for cold weather. English hat and Latvian cepure are broader and also include styles normally called шляпа. Do not replace it merely to use another valid hat word; specify the intended object. No шляпа option is present.

findings.suggestion: Keep батарейка for a small cell; specify that object rather than a phone battery
findings.reason: Батарейка is natural for a small replaceable battery/cell. In the phone/computer context a rechargeable internal battery is usually аккумулятор. The broad English battery does not establish which is intended. This is a context clarification, not a blanket replacement.

findings.suggestion: Use торт for a whole cake, or retain пирожное and clarify a small individual cake/pastry
findings.reason: Пирожное normally means an individual small cake/pastry, while generic English cake and Latvian kūka do not force that size/type. Decide the intended item across languages before changing the Russian. The attempted Gramota пирожное page did not expose a dictionary definition in retrieval; source verification is still needed.

findings.suggestion: Keep сумка for a bag carried as an item; use пакет only if a shopping carrier bag is intended
findings.reason: Сумка is a normal everyday bag. A shopping checkout request often means пакет, and Japanese 袋 likewise points toward a sack/bag rather than necessarily a handbag. The bare meaning bag is broad, so this is a sense decision, not evidence that сумка is wrong. No пакет distractor is present.

findings.suggestion: Keep карта; clarify payment/bank card in the shopping context if that is the teaching intent
findings.reason: Карта is natural for a payment card and also has other senses, including map. No city-map distractor is in this actual question; do not report a collision with 0390 simply because that concept exists elsewhere.

findings.suggestion: Keep школьный рюкзак if a backpack is intended; clarify the schoolbag sense
findings.reason: A школьный рюкзак is specifically a school backpack. English schoolbag and Latvian skolas soma also cover other bags. It is a practical common object and does not require replacement solely for breadth; record the narrower sense.

findings.suggestion: Clarify phrase versus sentence with examples/context and replace the sentence distractor where it is defensible
findings.reason: Actual RU→EN question 0403 presents phrase as correct and sentence (0404) as a distractor. Gramota defines фраза as a relatively complete utterance and gives Заявление состояло из двух фраз; a sentence is a defensible translation of the bare Russian prompt. RU→LV also places frāze and teikums together. Do not claim all four choices are unambiguous because their strings differ.

findings.suggestion: Keep идти for go on foot in a single direction; clarify the broad English to go
findings.reason: Идти is a practical beginner verb, but it is not the generic verb for all travel (going by vehicle often uses ехать). Clarifying the walking-on-foot sense also helps preserve the distinct intended 0413 walking concept. Do not add motion-verb complexity solely for elegance.

findings.suggestion: ходить пешком for general walking, or retain гулять only with a leisure-walk sense agreed across languages
findings.reason: Гулять normally means take a walk/spend leisure time outside, not neutral locomotion by walking in every context. Gramota explicitly defines the leisure/rest sense. English to walk, Latvian staigāt and Japanese 歩く are broader. Any replacement must keep 0411 go on foot distinct; гулять itself is common and useful.

findings.suggestion: Review the 0433 watch/наблюдать distractor and supply the intended looking-versus-observing context
findings.reason: Actual EN→RU 0432 offers смотреть на and наблюдать, while RU→EN offers to look at and to watch. These meanings overlap for looking attentively at something; the bare English/Russian forms do not fully fix the intended distinction. This is a model-editorial ambiguity candidate requiring human adjudication, weaker than the dictionary-supported нога collision.

findings.suggestion: Keep наблюдать for observe/watch an event; clarify that this is not the general watch TV sense
findings.reason: Наблюдать is natural for observing someone or an event. Watching television usually uses смотреть. The current English to watch is broader; replacing it mechanically with смотреть would worsen the overlap with 0432. Resolve the senses and actual distractor set together.

findings.suggestion: Keep ты for one familiar person; explain вы as the polite/plural alternative when context is available
findings.reason: Ты agrees with Latvian tu but English you does not specify familiarity or number. The polite greeting and request forms elsewhere use the вы level. Ты is appropriate with peers and is not universally rude or wrong. No вы distractor is currently present.

findings.suggestion: Keep этот for masculine this + noun; review это if the standalone meaning this thing is intended
findings.reason: Этот is a masculine demonstrative determiner/pronoun and agrees with Latvian šis. Bare English this and Japanese これ can suggest the standalone это sense. Do not replace the established masculine form without deciding the shared sense; current other choices do not create a second clear answer.

findings.suggestion: Keep тот for masculine that + noun; review то/это only after choosing the standalone demonstrative sense
findings.reason: Тот agrees with Latvian tas as a masculine demonstrative. Standalone English that can instead correspond to то or это depending on context. This needs a grammatical/situational label, not a declaration that тот is an uncommon word.

notes: Reviewed every one of the 510 Russian forms against the stated meaning, all supplied language forms and all three actual distractors in dist/audit-input.json. Relevant selectable directions are en-ru, lv-ru, ru-en and ru-lv; Japanese comparisons inform shared-sense consistency but ru-ja/ja-ru are not enabled.
Unflagged entries are working keeps for this model/editorial pass, not fluent-human certification. No claim of corpus-derived frequency rank or learner effectiveness is made.

0001 здравствуйте already matches the owner-requested neutral/polite hello default. No Russian greeting correction is proposed there. Привет is a valid casual alternative, but it is not the current entry.

Mать and отец (0017/0018) are valid ordinary relationship nouns. Мама and папа are natural familiar alternatives, not mandatory corrections. Similarly картофель, курятина, зарядное устройство and стопа are valid useful forms; the existence of a conversational synonym alone does not establish an error.

Russian masculine dictionary adjective/person forms are retained as teaching lemmas; ordinary inflection is not by itself a vocabulary error. No changes proposed solely to add formal grammar, punctuation or stylistic variety.

Source-supported flags describe the cited dictionary senses and their concrete collision or mismatch. Choice of beginner teaching default in model-editorial findings still needs fluent-human review. Sources on a model-editorial finding support only the lexical background, not a measured commonness claim.

Gramota dictionary definitions were retrieved for нога, гулять, фраза, жажда, извинить and лихорадка. The пирожное retrieval returned a page without usable definition; its finding is explicitly source-needed/editorial. No unverified dictionary URL is presented as supporting that claim.
Findings are proposals only. Active vocabulary, answer bindings, reading guides, recordings, code and publication were not changed.
